title: Wood, rubber and metal clarinets compared
summary: He prefers wood, compares rubber, and relays Bill Russell's remark that material makes no tonal difference; his museum clarinet was out of line.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Um, do you have any feelings about which make of clarinets you like best?

I like a wooden clarinet the best. But before I got this, this ram system, I used it as rubber clarinet. I got the same thing out of the rubber clarinet as I did the wood. But the wood, it gets better. Because you're not, if you drop the rubber, you know, that's not a very tall, ever. You put half a piece off. You see? And you got to be careful with the wood. You might bend the keys and something, you know, pull it out of the line. You don't break that even.

Yeah. I know Bill Russell was talking about different instruments the other day and saying that they reckon now these classical musicians and so on that there really isn't any difference in tone at all between a metal or a wood or whatever.
